default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) が: 「が」 marks a subject or the thing being described, but in 「子どもが落とす」, 「子ども」 would become the subject of “drop,” which does not fit this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) に: 「に」 commonly marks a place, time, or direction, but 「自分の子どもに落とす」 cannot express the intended meaning “drop one’s own cubs.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) で: 「で」 commonly marks the place or means of an action, but the starting point is already expressed by 「高いところから」, and 「子どもで落とす」 is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.why.0: ✗ (a) か: か is used to form a question or express uncertainty, so 食べるか太りますよ does not express the conditional relationship required in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.why.1: ✗ (b) を: を marks the object of a verb, but 甘いもの is already the object of 食べる; 食べるを太りますよ is an incorrect connection.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.why.2: ✗ (c) が: が usually marks the subject or connects clauses with a contrastive meaning, so 食べるが太りますよ cannot form the meaning “if you eat, you will gain weight.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q2.why.3: ✓ (d) と: と connects 食べる and 太ります to express a natural or expected result of eating too many sweet things: “if you eat them, you will gain weight.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.why.0: ✗ (a) よむ: 「よむおわったら」 is incorrect because よむ is the dictionary form and cannot directly connect to おわる in the pattern meaning “finish reading”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.why.1: ✓ (b) よみ: よみ is the stem of 読む after removing ます, so it can connect with おわる to form よみおわったら, meaning “after finishing reading”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.why.2: ✗ (c) よめ: よめ is the imperative form of 読む, meaning “read!”, so it cannot come before おわる to express “finish reading”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q3.why.3: ✗ (d) よんで: よんで is the て-form of 読む, but this pattern requires the ます-stem よみ before おわる, not よんでおわったら.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.why.0: ✓ (a) 壊れる: The dictionary form 壊れる correctly connects with 「ことがある」 in 「壊れることがある」, meaning “sometimes breaks down”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.why.1: ✗ (b) 壊れて: 壊れて is the て-form and cannot directly connect to 「ことがある」 to express “sometimes breaks down”; 壊れることがある is required.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.why.2: ✗ (c) 壊れた: 壊れた is the past form and would make 「壊れたことがある」 mean “has broken down before”, which does not fit the sentence’s meaning of something that happens sometimes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q4.why.3: ✗ (d) 壊れない: 壊れない means “does not break down”, which contradicts the idea that the machine sometimes breaks down and causes trouble.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.why.0: ✗ (a) ほど: ほど expresses a degree or approximate amount such as “to the extent of” or “about”, so it cannot naturally follow ジュースやサンドイッチ to mean “and so on” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.why.1: ✗ (b) しか: しか means “only” and normally requires a negative predicate; moreover, ジュースやサンドイッチしかを買いました is incorrect because しか cannot be used this way with the affirmative predicate 買いました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.why.2: ✓ (c) など: など means “and so on” or “similar things”, so ジュースやサンドイッチなどを買いました means “bought juice, sandwiches, and similar things”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q5.why.3: ✗ (d) だけ: だけ means “only”, so ジュースやサンドイッチだけを買いました would emphasize that the speaker bought only juice and sandwiches, rather than giving examples of items bought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.why.0: ✗ (a) で: 「石油で作られます」 uses 「で」 to indicate a material or means, but this sentence emphasizes that petroleum is transformed into plastic, so 「から」 is needed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.why.1: ✗ (b) を: 「を」 marks a direct object, but in 「石油（　）作られます」, 「石油」 is the source material, not the direct object of 「作られます」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.why.2: ✓ (c) から: 「石油から作られます」 means “is made from petroleum,” which correctly shows petroleum being transformed into plastic.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q6.why.3: ✗ (d) が: 「が」 marks the subject, but 「石油が作られます」 would mean “petroleum is made,” which contradicts the intended meaning that plastic is made from petroleum.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.why.0: ✓ (a) 結婚し: 「結婚し」is the stem of 「結婚します」, so it correctly connects to 「たがっています」to express another person’s desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.why.1: ✗ (b) 結婚して: 「結婚して」is the て-form of 「結婚する」, and it does not directly connect to 「たがっています」in this pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.why.2: ✗ (c) 結婚する: 「結婚する」is the dictionary form, but the form required before 「たがっています」is the verb stem 「結婚し」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q7.why.3: ✗ (d) 結婚しよう: 「結婚しよう」is the volitional form, meaning “let’s marry” or “I/we will marry,” so it cannot be used before 「たがっています」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.why.0: ✗ (a) おこって: 「おこって」 is the て-form of 「おこる」, but 「だす」 in this sentence must follow the verb stem 「おこり」, not the て-form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.why.1: ✗ (b) おこる: 「おこる」 is the dictionary form, but 「～だす」 here requires the stem form 「おこり」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.why.2: ✗ (c) おこた: 「おこた」 is not a correct conjugated form of 「おこる」, so it cannot be followed by 「だした」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q8.why.3: ✓ (d) おこり: 「おこり」 is the stem form of 「おこります」, so it correctly combines with 「だした」 to form 「おこりだした」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.why.0: ✗ (a) 行き: 「行き」is the continuative stem of 「行く」 and cannot be placed directly before 「つもりです」 to express an intention not to go; 「行きつもりです」is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.why.1: ✓ (b) 行かない: 「行かない」is the negative form of 「行く」 and correctly connects with 「つもりです」in the pattern 「～ないつもりです」, meaning “intend not to go.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.why.2: ✗ (c) 行こう: 「行こう」is the volitional form and can express an intention or invitation, but it does not connect directly to 「つもりです」; 「行こうつもりです」is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q9.why.3: ✗ (d) 行かないで: 「行かないで」means “without doing…” or “don’t do…,” and it cannot be placed directly before 「つもりです」; 「行かないでつもりです」is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.why.0: ✗ (a) 多い: 多い is the dictionary form of an い-adjective and cannot connect directly to なりました; it must change to 多くなりました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.why.1: ✗ (b) 多かった: 多かった is the past form of 多い, so 多かったなりました is an incorrect connection; the sentence needs 多くなりました to express becoming more frequent.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.why.2: ✓ (c) 多く: 多く is the correct form before なりました, forming 多くなりました, which means “became more numerous” or “became more frequent.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q10.why.3: ✗ (d) 多くない: 多くない means “not many,” but “became not many” would be expressed as 多くなくなりました; 多くないなりました is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.why.0: ✗ (a) のが: 「のが」 nominalizes a clause and marks it as the subject, so 「いい天気のが」 cannot form the intended conditional expression here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.why.1: ✓ (b) なら: 「なら」 follows a noun or noun phrase such as 「いい天気」 to express the condition “if the weather is good.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.why.2: ✗ (c) は: 「は」 marks a topic or contrast, so 「いい天気は」 does not clearly express the condition “if the weather is good” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q11.why.3: ✗ (d) では: 「では」 usually expresses contrast or a situation such as “in that case,” but 「いい天気では」 is not the natural way to state the condition here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.why.0: ✗ (a) 帰る: 「帰る」is the dictionary form, but the advice pattern 「Vたほうがいい」requires the verb in the past form 「帰った」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.why.1: ✗ (b) 帰って: 「帰って」is the て-form, which is commonly used to connect actions or make requests; it is not the form used in 「Vたほうがいい」in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.why.2: ✓ (c) 帰った: 「帰ったほうがいい」correctly follows the pattern 「Vたほうがいい」and means “should go home,” which fits the advice to leave soon because it has started raining.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q12.why.3: ✗ (d) 帰り: 「帰り」is the stem form of 「帰る」, but it cannot directly form 「帰りほうがいい」; the correct expression is 「帰ったほうがいい」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.why.0: ✗ (a) そして: そして usually connects actions or events in sequence; this sentence needs a word that adds another advantage, “the price is also low,” so それに is more natural.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.why.1: ✓ (b) それに: それに means “moreover” or “in addition” and is used here to add the information that the skirt is also inexpensive.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.why.2: ✗ (c) それで: それで expresses a result or a consequence, but “the price is also low” is an additional advantage here, not a result.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q13.why.3: ✗ (d) それが: それが usually means “but that...” or refers to a particular matter, so it cannot naturally connect to the added idea “the price is also low” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.why.0: ✓ (a) 食べる: The dictionary-form verb 「食べる」 comes before 「ようにしています」 to express trying to develop or maintain the habit of eating many vegetables.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.why.1: ✗ (b) 食べて: 「食べて」 is the て-form, which cannot be used directly in 「Vるようにしています」 to express trying to maintain a habit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.why.2: ✗ (c) 食べた: 「食べた」 is the past form, so it does not fit because the sentence describes a habit the speaker is currently trying to maintain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q14.why.3: ✗ (d) 食べます: 「食べます」 is the polite form; before 「ようにしています」, the plain dictionary form 「食べる」 is required, not the 「ます」 form.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.why.0: ✓ (a) する: 「するために」 uses the dictionary form of the verb before 「ために」 to express the purpose of going abroad, namely “to study design.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.why.1: ✗ (b) し: 「し」 is the connective form of 「する」 and cannot be placed directly before 「ために」 in this purpose pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.why.2: ✗ (c) した: 「したために」 usually expresses a cause or reason for a result, so it does not fit the intended meaning of going abroad “to study design.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q15.why.3: ✗ (d) しよう: 「しよう」 is the volitional form of 「する」, but this purpose structure requires the dictionary form 「する」 before 「ために」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.why.0: ✗ (a) ので: ので means “because” and expresses a reason, but this sentence needs to show the contrast between waiting for the call and the call not coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.why.1: ✗ (b) から: から also means “because,” so it cannot express the contrast intended in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.why.2: ✗ (c) のが: のが nominalizes an action or emphasizes its subject, but “待っているのが、かかってきません” does not form a grammatically appropriate connection here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q16.why.3: ✓ (d) のに: のに means “although/even though,” so it appropriately connects “waiting for a phone call from him” with the unexpected result that “the call does not come.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.why.0: ✗ (a) あるく: あるく is the dictionary form and cannot directly precede にくい; it must change to the verb stem あるき.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.why.1: ✓ (b) あるき: あるき is the ます-stem of あるく, so it correctly combines with にくい to form あるきにくい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.why.2: ✗ (c) あるいて: あるいて is the て-form of あるく, and it is not used before にくい in this grammar pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q17.why.3: ✗ (d) あるいた: あるいた is the past form of あるく, so it cannot directly combine with にくい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.why.0: ✓ (a) を — を marks 心配 as what the speaker caused in the fixed expression 心配をかける, so the sentence means “I made my parents worry.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.why.1: ✗ (b) も — も means “also,” but it cannot replace を to mark 心配 as the object in the fixed expression 心配をかける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.why.2: ✗ (c) で — で usually marks a place, means, or method, so 心配でかけました does not form the correct expression for “make someone worry.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q18.why.3: ✗ (d) は — は marks a topic or contrast, but here 心配 is the direct object of かける and must take を in the expression 心配をかける.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.why.0: ✗ (a) のが: 「のが」nominalizes the preceding clause and marks it as the subject, as in 「～のが上手です」; here, it does not express the cause-and-result relationship between being taught and improving.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.why.1: ✗ (b) のに: 「のに」means “although/even though” and expresses a contrast; this sentence does not contrast 「教えていただいた」with 「上手になりました」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.why.2: ✓ (c) ので: 「ので」means “because,” linking 「せんぱいにいろいろ教えていただいた」as the cause of 「上手になりました」, so it fits the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q19.why.3: ✗ (d) のは: 「のは」turns the preceding clause into a topic for explanation or emphasis; it does not mean “because,” so it cannot naturally connect to 「上手になりました」 here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.why.0: ✗ (a) 行く: 「行く」 is the dictionary form, but the pattern 「ばかりです」 meaning “have just done” requires the past form 「行った」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.why.1: ✗ (b) 行って: 「行って」 is the て-form and cannot directly connect to 「ばかりです」 to mean “have just gone”; this sentence needs 「行ったばかりです」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.why.2: ✓ (c) 行った: 「行った」 is the past form of 「行く」 and forms 「行ったばかりです」, meaning “have just gone,” which fits the trip to Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q20.why.3: ✗ (d) 行こう: 「行こう」 is the volitional form, meaning “let’s go” or “will go,” so it cannot be used in 「Vたばかりです」 to describe a completed trip.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.why.0: ✗ (a) べんりで: 「べんりでので」 is an incorrect connection; a な-adjective must use 「べんりなので」 before 「ので」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.why.1: ✗ (b) べんり: 「べんりので」 is missing 「な」, so it cannot correctly connect to 「ので」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.why.2: ✗ (c) べんりだ: 「べんりだので」 is incorrect; before 「ので」, a な-adjective uses 「な」 instead of 「だ」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q21.why.3: ✓ (d) べんりな: 「べんりな」 combines with 「ので」 to form 「べんりなので」, expressing that the tape recorder is light and convenient.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.why.0: ✗ (a) を: を is already used in 「映画を」 to mark “the movie” as the object of 見る; 「見を行きました」 is not a correct pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.why.1: ✓ (b) に: に connects the verb stem 見 with 行きました in the pattern 「Vます + に行く」, expressing the purpose of going: going to see a movie.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.why.2: ✗ (c) は: は marks a topic or contrast, so 「見は行きました」 does not form a correct grammatical pattern in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q22.why.3: ✗ (d) や: や is used to list nouns, such as 「映画や本」, and cannot connect 見る with 行きました to express purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.why.0: ✗ (a) くらべ: 「くらべ」 is normally used in patterns such as 「AとBをくらべる」 or 「Aにくらべて」, so it cannot be placed directly after 「今年」 to form this negative comparison.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.why.1: ✓ (b) ほど: In the pattern 「AはBほど～ない」, 「ほど」 follows the comparison standard 「今年」 and combines with 「暑くなかった」, so it is correct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.why.2: ✗ (c) ていど: 「程度」 means “degree” or “extent” and is not used in the negative comparison pattern 「Bほど～ない」; 「今年程度暑くなかった」 does not express the intended meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q23.why.3: ✗ (d) にで: 「にで」 is an invalid combination of particles in this position and cannot form a comparison with 「暑くなかった」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.why.0: ✗ (a) に: に cannot express the purpose “so as to catch the train” in 電車に間に合う; ように is needed in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.why.1: ✗ (b) から: から means “because” or “from,” so 電車に間に合うから would mean “because I catch the train,” which does not express the intended reason for getting up early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.why.2: ✓ (c) ように: ように connects with 電車に間に合う to express the purpose “so as to catch the 5 o’clock train.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q24.why.3: ✗ (d) を: を marks a direct object or, with some verbs, a route; it cannot follow 電車に間に合う to express purpose.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.why.0: ✓ (a) も: 「さかなもにくも」 means “both fish and meat,” which correctly shows that the dish uses both ingredients.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.why.1: ✗ (b) が: 「さかながにくが」 does not form a listing pattern meaning “both fish and meat”; 「が」 marks a subject or highlights a subject.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.why.2: ✗ (c) か: 「さかなかにくか」 expresses a choice, “fish or meat,” which conflicts with the sentence’s meaning that it uses both.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t20-q25.why.3: ✗ (d) で: 「さかなでにくで」 cannot connect the two ingredients to mean “both fish and meat”; 「で」 usually indicates a place, means, or method.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.why.0: ✗ (a) で: 「で」usually marks a means, place, or scope of an action; 「1週間で2回」is not the standard way to express the frequency “twice a week” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.why.1: ✓ (b) に: 「1週間に2回」is the correct expression for saying that the action happens twice within one week.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) は: 「は」marks a topic or contrast, so 「1週間は2回」cannot express the frequency of taking English conversation lessons.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) も: 「も」means “also” or “even,” so 「1週間も2回」does not convey the intended meaning “twice a week” here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.why.0: ✓ (a) 行った: 「行ったことがあります」 means “have been” or “have gone before,” expressing a past experience.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.why.1: ✗ (b) 行く: 「行くことがあります」 usually describes something that sometimes happens or an occasion when one goes, not the experience of having gone before in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.why.2: ✗ (c) 行って: 「行ってことがあります」 is grammatically incorrect because the て-form 「行って」 cannot directly connect to 「ことがあります」 in the experience pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q2.why.3: ✗ (d) 行こう: 「行こうことがあります」 is incorrect because 「行こう」 is the volitional form and is not used before 「ことがあります」 in this pattern.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.why.0: ✗ (a) いて: 「いて」 is not the correct connecting form of the adjective 「いそがしい」; 「いそがし いて」 cannot be used in this sentence.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q9.why.3: ✗ (d) から: 「から」 can also express a reason, but the correct form is 「いそがしいから」; 「いそがしから」 is incorrect in this sentence.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q10.why.2: ✗ (c) までで: 「までで」 indicates a limit or an ending point, so it cannot express the purpose of making the books easy to find in this sentence.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.why.2: ✗ (c) から: から means “from” and marks a starting point; おそくから is unsuitable because this sentence needs to express the endpoint of the work.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q11.why.3: ✓ (d) まで: まで means “until” and combines with おそく to form おそくまで, meaning “until late,” which fits the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.why.0: ✗ (a) に: 「空に飛ぶ」 is not suitable here because に usually marks a destination or target, while 「飛ぶ」 in this sentence describes flying through the sky.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.why.2: ✓ (c) を: 「空を飛ぶ」 uses を to mark the space or route through which the bird flies; this is the correct usage in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q12.why.3: ✗ (d) から: 「空から飛ぶ」 would mean something like “fly from the sky,” marking the starting point, which does not match the intended meaning of flying in the sky.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.why.0: ✓ (a) まま: 「帰ったまま」means that after he returned to his country, he has remained in that state; specifically, he still has not returned to the company.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.why.1: ✗ (b) はず: 「帰ったはず」means “he should have returned” or “he is expected to have returned,” expressing an assumption rather than the continuing state of having returned and not coming back.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q13.why.2: ✗ (c) ように: 「帰ったように」usually means “as if he returned” or relates to manner or purpose, so it does not express that he has still not returned to the company.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q15.why.0: ✗ (a) ならっている means “is learning” and does not form the conditional advice pattern needed after 歌が上手になりたければ.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q18.why.0: ✓ (a) でも: コーヒーでも飲んでから means “let’s have coffee or something similar before we go,” which fits a gentle suggestion.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q19.why.3: ✗ (d) のか: 飲むのか expresses a question or uncertainty such as “whether someone will drink,” so 飲むのか使えません cannot express a purpose of use.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.why.0: ✗ (a) こと: こと means “thing/matter” or “the act of doing,” so 彼はひまなことです cannot express the inference that he is expected to be free.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q20.why.2: ✗ (c) ところ: ところ means “place” or “point/stage,” and ひまなところです does not express an inference based on tomorrow being a day off.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.why.1: ✗ (b) ために: ために means “in order to” or “because of”, but 修理するためにむりです does not express the intended meaning that repairing it is impossible.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.why.2: ✓ (c) のは: のは turns 修理する into “repairing it” and makes that action the topic, which correctly connects with むりです.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q21.why.3: ✗ (d) ものは: ものは cannot naturally nominalize 修理する in this sentence; 修理するものはむりです would have a different structure and would not mean “repairing it is impossible”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q22.why.0: ✓ (a) 見つけられて: This is the passive form of 見つける (to find), meaning “be found”; it correctly describes the car being found by the police.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.why.2: ✗ (c) おいた: 「消えておいた」 does not fit because 「～ておく」 expresses doing something in advance or preparing something, whereas the fire goes out rather than being prepared to go out.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q23.why.3: ✓ (d) いった: 「消えていった」 means that the fire gradually went out, which fits 「だんだん」 in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.why.0: ✗ (a) のを: 「知るのを」 nominalizes 「知る」 and marks it as an object, but it does not express “useful for learning about Japan” in the pattern 「役に立つ」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.why.1: ✓ (b) のに: 「知るのに役に立ちます」 uses the pattern 「Vる + のに役に立つ」, meaning “to be useful for doing something.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.why.2: ✗ (c) ものが: 「ものが」 means “a thing/object” with the particle 「が」, so 「知るものが役に立ちます」 does not express that the book is useful for learning about Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q24.why.3: ✗ (d) ものに: 「ものに」 cannot replace the purpose pattern 「Vる + のに役に立つ」; 「知るものに役に立ちます」 is also grammatically unsuitable in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.why.0: ✓ (a) 見ないで: 「見ないでください」 means “please do not watch,” which fits the context that it is time to go to bed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.why.1: ✗ (b) 見ていないで: 「見ていないでください」 describes a state of “please do not be not watching,” so it does not express the intended request not to watch TV here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.why.2: ✗ (c) 見ずに: 「見ずに」 means “without watching...” and normally needs to connect to another action, so it cannot be used directly with 「ください」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t21-q25.why.3: ✗ (d) 見ずで: 「見ずで」 is not the correct connection for this sentence; if the 「ず」 form is used, it should be 「見ずに」, but that still does not form the requested 「ください」 pattern here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.why.0: ✗ (a) 買うと: 買うと usually expresses an automatic or predictable result when something is done, so it does not fit the advice about going to Akihabara in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.why.1: ✓ (b) 買うなら: 買うなら means “if you want to buy” or “if you are planning to buy,” which appropriately introduces the advice to go to Akihabara for inexpensive electrical products.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) 買えば: 買えば means “if you buy,” but it would make the sentence mean “if you buy inexpensive electrical products, you should go to Akihabara,” reversing the intended relationship between the two actions.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) 買って: 買って is the て-form of 買う, used to connect actions or make requests, so it does not express the condition “if you want to buy” here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.why.0: ✗ (a) ままが: まま describes keeping a state unchanged, but 飲まないままがいい does not form the appropriate advice pattern in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.why.1: ✗ (b) ずつで: ずつ means “each,” “at a time,” or “in equal portions” and normally follows an amount or counter, so it cannot directly follow 飲まない here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.why.2: ✓ (c) ほうが: 飲まないほうがいいですよ is the Vないほうがいい pattern, meaning “it is better not to drink,” which fits the meaning of this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q2.why.3: ✗ (d) ほどで: ほど expresses degree or extent, but 飲まないほどで does not form an advice structure, and the particle で is also unsuitable here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.why.0: ✗ (a) よりも: よりも is used for comparison and means “more than,” so だれよりも would mean “more than whom,” which does not ask who thought of 電灯.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.why.1: ✗ (b) でも: でも can mean “also” or “even,” so だれでも means “anyone,” not the agent who carried out the action 考え出された.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.why.2: ✓ (c) によって: によって follows だれ to mark the agent in a passive sentence, so だれによって means “by whom” the electric light was thought up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q3.why.3: ✗ (d) で: で usually marks a place or means, so だれで cannot naturally mark the person who performed the action in this passive sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.why.0: ✓ (a) で: で marks “厚い紙” as the material used to make the shoes, fitting the pattern “Nで作られている” (be made of N).
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q4.why.1: ✗ (b) と: と does not mark the material in this sentence; “厚い紙と作られている” cannot express “made of thick paper.”

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.why.0: ✓ (a) より: 「何より好きなもの」 means “the thing I like more than anything,” which fits the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t22-q5.why.1: ✗ (b) から: 「何から好きなもの」 does not form a grammatical pattern meaning “like the most” in this sentence.
