default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.why.0: ✗ (a) わたして: わたして is the て-form of 渡す, so it cannot be placed in the pattern 「お＋verb stem＋いたします」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.why.1: ✗ (b) わたす: わたす is the dictionary form of 渡す, but this sentence requires the verb stem, わたし.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.why.2: ✗ (c) わたせ: わたせ is the imperative form of 渡す, meaning “hand it over,” so it does not fit with 「いたします」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q11.why.3: ✓ (d) わたし: わたし is the verb stem of 渡します after removing ます, forming 「お渡しいたします」, meaning “I will humbly hand/give it to you.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.why.0: ✗ (a) 読めて: 「読めて」is the て-form of the potential verb 「読める」, so it cannot come before 「かた」to form the required word 「読みかた」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.why.1: ✗ (b) 読んで: 「読んで」is the て-form of 「読む」, and this て-form does not combine with 「かた」in the expression needed here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.why.2: ✗ (c) 読む: 「読む」is the dictionary form of the verb, but the noun-forming expression before 「かた」requires 「読み」to make 「読みかた」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q12.why.3: ✓ (d) 読み: 「読み」is the continuative form of 「読む」and combines with 「かた」to make 「読みかた」, meaning “the way of reading.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.why.0: ✗ (a) が: が marks the subject, so 友だちが would mean “the friend...” as the subject and would not express “I showed my friend the photos.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.why.1: ✗ (b) で: で marks the place or means of an action; 友だちで cannot indicate the person who is shown the photos.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.why.2: ✓ (c) に: に marks the person affected by or receiving the action 見せる; 友だちに means “to my friend” or “my friend.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q13.why.3: ✗ (d) から: から means “from” and marks a source or starting point; 友だちから does not fit the meaning of showing the photos to a friend.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.why.0: ✗ (a) へ: へ indicates a direction or destination, so it cannot connect “田中さん” with “来る日” to show who performs the action of coming.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.why.1: ✗ (b) を: を marks the object of a verb, but “田中さん” is the subject of 来る, not an object receiving an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.why.2: ✗ (c) で: で commonly indicates a place, means, or method, so it cannot express the modifying relationship between “田中さん” and “来る日”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q14.why.3: ✓ (d) の: の connects the noun “田中さん” with “来る日” and means “the day Tanaka comes,” so it fits this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.why.0: ✓ (a) しか — 「よやくした人しか入れません」 means “only people who made a reservation can enter,” and 「しか」 is correctly used with the negative form 「入れません」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.why.1: ✗ (b) から — 「よやくした人から入れません」 does not express “only people who made a reservation can enter”; 「から」 usually means “from” or “because”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.why.2: ✗ (c) より — 「よやくした人より入れません」 does not express a restriction on who may enter; 「より」 is usually used for comparison or a starting point.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q15.why.3: ✗ (d) ぐらい — 「よやくした人ぐらい入れません」 does not mean “only”; 「ぐらい」 usually expresses an approximate amount or degree.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.why.0: ✗ (a) が: どれが means “which one” when asking about or identifying a particular item, but どれが高くて買えなかった does not express that all the bags were expensive here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.why.1: ✓ (b) も: どれも means “all of them” and emphasizes that every bag was expensive; therefore, the speaker could not buy one.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.why.2: ✗ (c) でも: どれでも usually means “any one/whichever one,” expressing an unrestricted choice rather than the meaning that all the bags were expensive in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q16.why.3: ✗ (d) ばかり: ばかり can mean “only,” “nothing but,” or “just,” but どればかり is not the appropriate expression for saying that all the bags were expensive here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.why.0: ✗ (a) や: や connects nouns such as お金や時間, but it cannot connect the two clauses お金もない and 時間もない in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.why.1: ✗ (b) で: で cannot directly connect the negative clause お金もない to 時間もない to list reasons in this structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.why.2: ✓ (c) し: し connects clauses to give multiple reasons; お金もないし、時間もないから means “there is no money, and there is also no time.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q17.why.3: ✗ (d) とか: とか is used to give examples or an incomplete list, so お金もないとか does not appropriately connect the two specific reasons here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.why.0: ✗ (a) が／が: 「が」 does not connect two choices in the pattern 「AとBとどちらが好きですか」, so 「するのが、見るのがどちらが好きですか」 is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.why.1: ✓ (b) と／と: 「と」 follows both 「スポーツをするの」 and 「見るの」, forming the correct pattern 「AとBとどちらが好きですか」 to ask which activity is preferred.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.why.2: ✗ (c) や／や: 「や」 lists examples in a non-exhaustive way, but this sentence asks the learner to choose between two activities with 「どちら」, so 「や／や」 is not appropriate.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q18.why.3: ✗ (d) も／も: 「も」 means “also” or “both,” and it does not connect two alternatives in the question pattern 「どちらが好きですか」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.why.0: ✗ (a) を: を does not mark the person being made or allowed to do something in the pattern ～に～をさせる; in this sentence, it follows しゅくだい to mark “homework.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.why.1: ✗ (b) が: が marks a subject or an emphasized element, but it does not mark 子ども as the person being made or allowed to act in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.why.2: ✗ (c) で: で usually marks a place or means, so 子どもで cannot express the meaning “make or let the child do homework.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q19.why.3: ✓ (d) に: に marks the person who performs the action in the causative pattern, so 子どもにしゅくだいをさせた means “made or let the child do homework.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.why.0: ✓ (a) 働く: 働く is the dictionary form of the verb and correctly combines with ために as 「働くために」, meaning “in order to work.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.why.1: ✗ (b) 働き: 働き is the verb stem or a noun form, so it cannot directly precede ために to express purpose in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.why.2: ✗ (c) 働いて: 働いて is the て-form, which is used to connect actions or form requests, not to express purpose before ために here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q20.why.3: ✗ (d) 働こう: 働こう is the volitional form, meaning “let’s work” or “I will work,” so it does not fit the purpose pattern 「Vるために」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.why.0: ✗ (a) 読むの: 「読むの」 is a nominalized or explanatory form, not the past form required before 「ことがありません」 to express “have never read”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.why.1: ✗ (b) 読んで: 「読んで」 is the て-form, used to connect actions or make requests; it does not form the experience pattern 「Vたことがありません」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.why.2: ✓ (c) 読んだ: 「読んだ」 is the past form of 「読む」 and correctly combines with 「ことがありません」 in 「読んだことがありません」, meaning “have never read”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q21.why.3: ✗ (d) 読みます: 「読みます」 is the polite present/future form of 「読む」, so it is not used before 「ことがありません」 in the experience pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.why.0: ✗ (a) ぐらい: 「子どものぐらい」 does not form a correct expression in this sentence; 「ぐらい」 usually indicates degree or quantity, not “like a child.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.why.1: ✓ (b) ように: 「子どものように」 means “like a child,” and it correctly describes how the mother 「よろこんだ」—rejoiced.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.why.2: ✗ (c) らしい: 「子どものらしい」 does not fit this sentence structure; 「らしい」 usually means “typical of” or “seems,” rather than directly describing the manner of rejoicing here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q22.why.3: ✗ (d) そうに: 「子どものそうに」 is an incorrect connection; 「そうに」 usually follows a verb stem or an adjective to express “seems,” and it does not follow 「子どもの」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.why.0: ✓ (a) いる: 「よごれている」uses the 「ている」pattern to describe the resulting state that the shirt is dirty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.why.1: ✗ (b) ある: 「よごれてある」is not used to describe a shirt being dirty; 「ある」usually expresses the existence of an inanimate thing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.why.2: ✗ (c) みる: 「よごれてみる」would mean “try to make something dirty,” which does not fit the meaning that the shirt is already dirty.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q23.why.3: ✗ (d) おく: 「よごれておく」would mean “leave something dirty” or “make something dirty in advance,” which does not fit the situation of washing the shirt.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.why.0: ✗ (a) やめる: 「やめるです」is grammatically incorrect; やめる needs to be combined with つもり to express an intention in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.why.1: ✓ (b) やめるつもり: 「やめるつもりです」correctly follows the pattern 「dictionary-form verb + つもりです」and means “intend to quit.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.why.2: ✗ (c) やめるだろう: 「やめるだろうです」incorrectly combines 「だろう」with 「です」; 「だろう」expresses a guess, not the speaker’s definite intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q24.why.3: ✗ (d) やめましょう: 「やめましょうです」is grammatically incorrect; 「やめましょう」means “let’s quit” or “we should quit,” so it does not fit before 「です」here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.why.0: ✗ (a) あると: 「～と」 usually expresses a natural or inevitable result; 「ひまが あると、あそびに 来て ください」 does not fit the invitation “please come and visit.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.why.1: ✗ (b) あって: 「あって」 is the て-form of ある and is generally used to connect actions or ideas; 「ひまが あって、あそびに 来て ください」 does not correctly express the condition “if you have free time.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.why.2: ✓ (c) あったら: 「～たら」 attaches to the past form, but 「ひまが あったら」 expresses the condition “if you have free time,” which fits the invitation to come and visit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t24-q25.why.3: ✗ (d) あったため: 「～ため」 expresses a cause or reason; 「ひまが あったため、あそびに 来て ください」 would mean “because you had free time, please come and visit,” which is unnatural and does not express the conditional meaning needed here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.why.0: ✗ (a) と: と usually marks quoted content or something done together with, so it cannot mark いい におい in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) を: を marks the object of an action, but におい in においがします is something being sensed, not the object of an action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) に: に can mark a place, time, or target, but here だいどころから already marks the source of the smell, so いい におい must be followed by が.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q1.why.3: ✓ (d) が: が marks いい におい, the pleasant smell being sensed in the pattern ～から～がします.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.why.0: ✗ (a) まで: 「まで」means “until” and usually describes an action or state continuing up to a time, so it does not precisely express the deadline for submitting the homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.why.1: ✓ (b) までに: 「までに」means “by” or “no later than,” which fits the requirement to 出して the homework by the 10th.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.why.2: ✗ (c) までは: 「までは」means “until” with emphasis on the time limit or contrast, but it does not fit naturally as the deadline expression in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q2.why.3: ✗ (d) までも: 「までも」means “even as far as” or “even until,” so it does not fit the specific deadline for submitting the homework.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.why.0: ✗ (a) で: で does not mark the content of a direct quotation in the pattern 「...」と言っていました, so 「また 電話します」で言っていました is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.why.1: ✗ (b) に: に can indicate the person receiving what is said, but it does not directly connect the quoted content 「また 電話します」 to 言っていました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.why.2: ✓ (c) と: と follows 「また 電話します」 and connects the quoted statement to 言っていました, meaning “said that he would call again.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q3.why.3: ✗ (d) か: か marks a question or uncertainty, but 「また 電話します」 is a definite statement, so 「...」か言っていました is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.why.0: ✓ (a) ばかり 「遊んでばかりで」means “only playing” or “doing nothing but playing,” which correctly contrasts with 「勉強をしない」(does not study).
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.why.1: ✗ (b) ぐらい 「遊んでぐらいで」does not form a correct grammar pattern; ぐらい usually means “about” or “to the extent that,” not “only.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.why.2: ✗ (c) しか 「遊んでしかで」cannot be connected this way; しか must be used with a negative form, such as 「遊んでしかいない」, and it does not come before で in this structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q4.why.3: ✗ (d) ながら 「遊んでながらで」has the wrong connection; ながら follows the verb stem, as in 「遊びながら」, meaning “while playing,” which does not fit the structure here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.why.0: ✗ (a) は: は marks the topic or contrast, so 「書いたは知っていますか」 cannot connect grammatically in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.why.1: ✗ (b) を: を marks a direct object, but 「だれがこの本を書いた」 is an indirect-question clause that must end with か, not を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.why.2: ✓ (c) か: か follows the clause 「だれがこの本を書いた」 and turns “who wrote this book” into an indirect question functioning as the object of 「知っていますか」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q5.why.3: ✗ (d) で: で indicates a place, means, or manner, so it cannot follow 「だれがこの本を書いた」 to form an indirect question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.why.0: ✓ (a) を — を is used in 空を飛んで行きました to mark the space that the airplane flies through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.why.1: ✗ (b) は — は marks the topic, but 空は飛んで行きました would mean “as for the sky, it flew away,” which does not fit this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.why.2: ✗ (c) で — で usually marks the place where an action occurs or the means used, but 空で does not correctly express the route the airplane flies through here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q6.why.3: ✗ (d) と — と usually means “and” or “with,” so 空と飛んで行きました cannot express the meaning “fly across the sky.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.why.0: ✗ (a) を: を is not used with 近い to mark the place or object that the apartment is close to; therefore 駅を近い is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.why.1: ✗ (b) の: の expresses possession or modifies a noun, but 駅の近い does not form the correct pattern for saying “close to the station.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.why.2: ✗ (c) で: で usually marks the place where an action occurs or a means of transportation, so it cannot be used with 近い to express proximity; 駅で近い is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q7.why.3: ✓ (d) に: に combines with 近い in the pattern Nに近い, and 駅に近い means “close to the station.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.why.0: ✗ (a) 聞く: 「聞く」 is the dictionary form and cannot be placed directly before 「たがる」; it must be changed to 「聞きたがる」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.why.1: ✓ (b) 聞き: 「聞き」 is the stem of 「聞きます」, so it correctly combines with 「たがる」 to form 「聞きたがる」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.why.2: ✗ (c) 聞いた: 「聞いた」 is the past form and cannot be used directly before 「たがる」; to express past desire, use 「聞きたがった」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q8.why.3: ✗ (d) 聞け: 「聞け」 is the imperative form meaning “listen,” so it cannot combine with 「たがる」 to express a desire.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.why.0: ✓ (a) する: 「する」is the dictionary form, which correctly connects with 「らしいです」to express that the two of them will get married next year.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.why.1: ✗ (b) した: 「した」is the past form and means “got married” or “did,” so it does not fit with 「らいねん」(next year).
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.why.2: ✗ (c) しよう: 「しよう」is the volitional form, meaning “let’s get married” or expressing the speaker’s intention, so it is not used to report hearsay with 「らしいです」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q9.why.3: ✗ (d) します: 「します」is the polite form, but 「らしいです」is preceded by the plain form, so 「します」cannot be used here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.why.0: ✗ (a) 行く: 「行く」 is the dictionary form and cannot directly connect to 「いつ…ても」 in this sentence; the て-form 「行って」 is required.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.why.1: ✗ (b) 行け: 「行け」 is the imperative form of 「行く」, meaning “Go!”, so it cannot be used in the pattern 「いつ…ても」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.why.2: ✗ (c) 行こう: 「行こう」 is the volitional form, meaning “Let’s go” or “I will go,” so it does not fit the pattern 「いつ…ても」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q10.why.3: ✓ (d) 行って: 「行って」 is the て-form of 「行く」 and combines with 「も」 in 「いつ行っても」, meaning “whenever one goes” or “no matter when one goes”.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.why.0: ✗ (a) 待たれさせた: 待たれさせた combines the forms unnaturally and does not correctly express the meaning “was made to wait.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.why.1: ✗ (b) 待たせさせた: 待たせさせた is a double-causative form, roughly meaning “made someone make another person wait,” so it does not describe the speaker being made to wait at the hospital.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.why.2: ✓ (c) 待たされた: This is the past form of 待たされる, meaning “was made to wait,” which fits the speaker’s experience of waiting at the hospital for one hour.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q11.why.3: ✗ (d) 待たされられた: 待たされられた incorrectly stacks causative and passive forms, so it is not the correct form for “was made to wait.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.why.0: ✓ (a) 開きます — 「開く」 is an intransitive verb meaning that the door opens by itself; 「開きます」 correctly fits the 「～と」 pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.why.1: ✗ (b) 開けます — 「開ける」 is a transitive verb meaning to open something; this sentence describes the door opening automatically, not someone opening it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.why.2: ✗ (c) 開いています — 「開いています」 means that the door is open or remains in an open state, but this sentence describes what happens after pressing here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q12.why.3: ✗ (d) 開けています — 「開けています」 means that someone is opening the door or has left it open using the transitive verb 「開ける」; this does not express the door opening automatically.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.why.0: ✓ (a) お帰りに なりました — お帰りになる is the respectful honorific form for describing 先生’s action of returning, and なりました makes it past and polite: “has returned.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.why.1: ✗ (b) お帰り なさいました — お帰りなさい is a greeting meaning “welcome home,” so お帰りなさいました is not the correct honorific form for saying that 先生 returned.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.why.2: ✗ (c) お帰り ございました — ございました is a polite form related to ござる/ある, so it cannot directly express the action of 先生 returning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q13.why.3: ✗ (d) お帰り いたしました — いたしました belongs to the humble pattern お〜いたす, which lowers the speaker’s own action; it should not be used for 先生’s action here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.why.0: ✗ (a) が — 「ことがなりました」 does not form a correct grammar pattern; 「が」 cannot connect 「こと」 to 「なりました」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.why.1: ✓ (b) に — 「ことになりました」 is a fixed pattern in which 「に」 follows 「こと」 to express that something has been decided or has come to be.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.why.2: ✗ (c) を — 「ことをなりました」 is grammatically incorrect; 「を」 cannot come before 「なりました」 in this pattern expressing a decision.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q14.why.3: ✗ (d) で — 「ことでなりました」 is not the correct connection; 「で」 is not used after 「こと」 to form 「ことになりました」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.why.0: ✓ (a) のに: いろいろさがしたのに見つからないんです means “Although I searched a lot, I still cannot find it,” which exactly expresses the contrast in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.why.1: ✗ (b) ので: ので means “because,” so いろいろさがしたので見つからないんです would mean “Because I searched a lot, I cannot find it,” which does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.why.2: ✗ (c) のを: のを nominalizes the preceding clause and marks it as an object, but いろいろさがしたのを見つからないんです does not form a correct structure for expressing “although I searched, I still cannot find it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q15.why.3: ✗ (d) のが: のが nominalizes the preceding clause and marks it as the subject, but いろいろさがしたのが見つからないんです does not express the contrast between searching and not finding something in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.why.0: ✗ (a) だけ: 「だけ」 means “only,” so 「姉のへやだけ」 would mean “only my older sister’s room”; it does not create the comparison “not as … as.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.why.1: ✗ (b) けど: 「けど」 means “but” and connects two contrasting clauses; 「姉のへやけど広くない」 does not form a correct comparison pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.why.2: ✓ (c) ほど: 「N1はN2ほど～ない」 means “N1 is not as ～ as N2”; 「わたしのへやは姉のへやほど広くない」 means that my room is not as spacious as my older sister’s room.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q16.why.3: ✗ (d) でも: 「でも」 can mean “also,” “even,” or “but,” but it is not used in the negative comparison pattern 「N1はN2ほど～ない」 here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.why.0: ✓ (a) も: Correct because も follows ５回 and emphasizes the surprisingly large number: “as many as five times.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.why.1: ✗ (b) が: Incorrect because が marks the subject and is not used after ５回 to express the number of times he read the novel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.why.2: ✗ (c) で: Incorrect because で usually marks a place, means, or scope; ５回で does not naturally mean “read five times” here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q17.why.3: ✗ (d) しか: Incorrect because しか means “only” and must be used with a negative predicate, such as 読んでいない; the sentence here is not negative.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.why.0: ✗ (a) の: の expresses possession or modification, so it cannot directly mark さいふ as the thing taken by とられた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.why.1: ✗ (b) に: に is already used after だれか to show who performed the action, so it cannot be used after さいふ in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.why.2: ✗ (c) か: か is used to form a question or mean “someone/something,” but さいふかとられた does not form the required grammatical pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q18.why.3: ✓ (d) を: を marks さいふ as the object taken in さいふをとられた, meaning “had one’s wallet taken.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.why.0: ✗ (a) では: 「持って来なくでは」 does not form the correct grammar pattern for saying that bringing the camera is unnecessary.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.why.1: ✗ (b) でも: 「持って来なくでも」 uses the wrong connection; the correct pattern is 「持って来なくてもかまいません」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.why.2: ✗ (c) ては: 「持って来なくては」 belongs to a different pattern and does not complete the permission expression meaning “you do not have to do it”; 「ても」 is needed here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q19.why.3: ✓ (d) ても: 「持って来なくてもかまいません」 is the correct pattern, meaning “it is okay not to bring the camera.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.why.0: ✗ (a) ならべて います: ならべる is a transitive verb meaning “to arrange something,” so it needs an object; this sentence describes people lining up by themselves, so ならべて います is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.why.1: ✗ (b) ならべて あります: ならべて あります describes something that has been arranged by someone, but 人 refers to people who are lining up, not objects that have been arranged.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.why.2: ✓ (c) ならんで います: ならぶ is an intransitive verb meaning “to line up,” so it correctly takes 人 as the subject; ならんで います describes the people’s ongoing state of lining up.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q20.why.3: ✗ (d) ならんで あります: ならぶ is an intransitive verb and does not combine with あります in this pattern; people who are lining up must be expressed with ならんで います.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.why.0: ✗ (a) 使います: This is the ordinary ます-form of 「使う」, meaning “use,” so it does not express the meaning “can use” required in this question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.why.1: ✓ (b) 使えます: This is the potential form of 「使います」, meaning “can use,” and it fits 「日本の お金が」 in this question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.why.2: ✗ (c) 使うんです: 「使うんです」adds an explanatory or emphatic nuance, “it is that one uses,” and does not ask whether Japanese money can be used here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q21.why.3: ✗ (d) 使ってです: 「使ってです」is an incorrect connection; 「使って」cannot be followed directly by 「です」 to express the ability to use something.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.why.0: ✗ (a) あって: 「あって」 is the て-form of 「ある」 and cannot be used directly before 「そうです」 in this hearsay pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.why.1: ✗ (b) あるだろう: 「あるだろう」 expresses the speaker’s guess “it will probably exist/take place,” but it does not fit the intended grammar pattern before 「そうです」 here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.why.2: ✗ (c) あった: 「あった」 is the past form of 「ある」 and means “there was,” which conflicts with 「らいしゅう」, meaning “next week.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q22.why.3: ✓ (d) ある: 「ある」 is the dictionary form of the verb and correctly comes before 「そうです」 in 「あるそうです」, meaning “I hear there will be.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.why.0: ✗ (a) およいで: およいで is the て-form of およぐ, usually used to connect actions or make requests, so it cannot express the change of ability required before ように なりました here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.why.1: ✗ (b) およいだ: およいだ is the past form meaning “swam,” but this sentence needs to express becoming able to swim.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.why.2: ✓ (c) およげる: およげる is the potential form of およぐ, meaning “can swim,” so it correctly fits the pattern ～ように なりました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q23.why.3: ✗ (d) およぎ: およぎ is the stem form of およぐ, which can connect to certain words, but it cannot directly precede ように なりました to express ability.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.why.0: ✗ (a) 話さなく: 「話さなく」 is the continuative form of the negative, which normally needs 「て」 or another following element; it cannot be used directly before 「ば」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.why.1: ✗ (b) 話さない: 「話さない」 is the ordinary negative form, but it must change to 「話さなけれ」 before 「ば」 to express the condition “if one does not speak.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.why.2: ✗ (c) 話さないで: 「話さないで」 means “without speaking” or “do not speak,” so it does not form the conditional pattern 「～なければ」 before 「ば」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t25-q24.why.3: ✓ (d) 話さなけれ: 「話さなけれ」 combines with 「ば」 to form 「話さなければ」, meaning “if one does not speak”; therefore, it is correct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.why.0: ✓ (a) わらわせる: It means “to make someone laugh”; the father says interesting things and makes everyone laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) わらいたい: It means “want to laugh,” describing someone’s desire to laugh rather than the father making everyone laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) わらわれる: It means “to be laughed at” or “to be ridiculed,” which is passive and opposite to the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) わらえる: It means “can laugh” or “be able to laugh,” and does not express making other people laugh.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.why.0: ✗ (a) むずかしい: 「むずかしいそうな」 is incorrect because 「～そうな」 cannot directly follow the full form 「むずかしい」 with 「い」 still attached.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.why.1: ✗ (b) むずかしいの: 「むずかしいのそうな」 is incorrect because 「の」 does not come between 「むずかしい」 and 「そうな」 in this pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.why.2: ✓ (c) むずかし: 「むずかしそうな」 is correct because 「むずかし」 is the stem of 「むずかしい」 and can connect to 「そうな」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q2.why.3: ✗ (d) むずかしく: 「むずかしくそうな」 is incorrect because 「むずかしく」 is the adverbial form, not the form used before 「そうな」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.why.0: ✓ (a) に: In this sentence, に marks the person who performed the action 注意された; しゃちょう is the person who reprimanded Tanaka.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.why.1: ✗ (b) の: の shows possession or modifies a noun, so しゃちょうのちゅういされた does not form the passive structure needed here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.why.2: ✗ (c) で: で usually marks a place or means of an action, but it does not mark the person who reprimanded someone in 注意された.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q3.why.3: ✗ (d) を: を marks the direct object of a verb, whereas しゃちょう is the person performing the reprimanding action here, so を is not used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.why.0: ✗ (a) が: が usually marks a subject or contrast, so it cannot follow 「どこへ行った」 to form the indirect question needed with 「わかりません」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.why.1: ✗ (b) の: の can nominalize a clause in some structures, but 「どこへ行ったのわかりません」 is missing か and does not form the correct “do not know ...” pattern here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.why.2: ✓ (c) か: か follows the question clause 「どこへ行った」 and forms 「どこへ行ったか わかりません」, meaning “I do not know where he went.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q4.why.3: ✗ (d) を: を marks a direct object, while the destination in this sentence is already marked by へ; を cannot connect this clause to 「わかりません」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.why.0: ✗ (a) か: か expresses a choice such as “or,” so ペンか書いてください does not correctly connect “pen” with the action of writing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.why.1: ✗ (b) の: の connects nouns to show possession or modification, but in ペンの書いてください it cannot connect ペン to the verb 書いてください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.why.2: ✗ (c) が: が marks a subject or highlights an object, but ペンが書いてください would make ペン seem to be the thing that writes, which is not the intended meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q5.why.3: ✓ (d) で: で follows a noun to indicate the tool or means used for an action; ペンで書いてください means “Please write with a pen.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.why.0: ✗ (a) でも: 「でも」 usually means “but” or “even,” and 「見てでもいる」 cannot express the idea of continually watching TV in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.why.1: ✓ (b) ばかり: 「見てばかりいる」 means “do nothing but watch,” which fits the warning that watching TV constantly can worsen your eyesight.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.why.2: ✗ (c) しか: 「しか」 must be used with a negative predicate to mean “only,” so 「見てしかいる」 is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q6.why.3: ✗ (d) ぐらい: 「ぐらい」 expresses an approximate degree or amount, so it cannot follow 「見て」 to show a repeated or prolonged action here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.why.0: ✗ (a) へ: へ indicates a direction or destination, so としょかんの まえへ 通る does not correctly express “pass in front of the library.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.why.1: ✗ (b) で: で usually marks the place where an action occurs, but 通る takes を here to mark the place or route that is passed through.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.why.2: ✗ (c) に: に can indicate a destination or a time, but としょかんの まえに 通る is not the correct way to express “pass in front of the library.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q7.why.3: ✓ (d) を: を follows としょかんの まえ to mark the place or route that the bus passes through; としょかんの まえを 通る is the correct expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.why.0: ✗ (a) で: で indicates a place or means, but “カメラでぬすまれて” does not correctly mark the object stolen in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.why.1: ✗ (b) に: に can indicate the agent in a passive sentence, but “カメラにぬすまれて” would make カメラ sound like the thief, so the meaning is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.why.2: ✓ (c) を: を marks カメラ as the direct object of ぬすむ, so “カメラをぬすまれてしまいました” is grammatically correct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q8.why.3: ✗ (d) へ: へ indicates a direction, but “カメラへぬすまれて” does not work with the verb ぬすむ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.why.0: ✗ (a) だけ: だけ means “only,” so 10本だけ飲んだ means “drank only ten bottles”; it does not express the emphasis on drinking as many as ten bottles.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.why.1: ✓ (b) も: 10本も飲んだ means “drank as many as ten bottles,” emphasizing an unusually large amount and matching the result 頭がいたい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.why.2: ✗ (c) しか: しか must be used with a negative predicate, such as しか飲まなかった, so 10本しか飲んだので is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q9.why.3: ✗ (d) でも: でも usually means “even” or “for example,” but 10本でも飲んだので does not naturally emphasize the large amount in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.why.0: ✗ (a) 入るは: 「入る」 is the dictionary form and cannot connect directly with 「いけません」 to make the prohibition pattern 「Vてはいけません」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.why.1: ✓ (b) 入っては: 「入って」 is the て-form of 「入る」, and with 「いけません」 it forms 「入ってはいけません」, meaning “must not enter.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.why.2: ✗ (c) 入りますは: 「入ります」 is the polite form, not the て-form 「入って」, so 「入りますはいけません」 does not form a correct grammar pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q10.why.3: ✗ (d) 入らないは: 「入らない」 is the negative form and is not used with 「いけません」 to express this prohibition; the correct form is 「入ってはいけません」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.why.0: ✗ (a) 歩いた: 「歩いた」 is the past form meaning “walked,” so it cannot be placed before 「なさい」 to make the request in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.why.1: ✗ (b) 歩く: 「歩く」 is the dictionary form meaning “to walk,” but 「なさい」 must be connected to the stem 「歩き」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.why.2: ✓ (c) 歩き: 「歩き」 is the stem of 「歩きます」 after removing 「ます」, so it correctly forms 「歩きなさい」 with 「なさい」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q11.why.3: ✗ (d) 歩け: 「歩け」 is the plain imperative form of 「歩く」, so it is not used together with 「なさい」 in this structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.why.0: ✗ (a) ほめさせて: ほめさせて is the て-form of the causative form, meaning “let or make someone praise,” so it cannot be directly followed by ました in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.why.1: ✓ (b) ほめられ: ほめられ is the stem of the passive form ほめられる, and it combines with ました to make ほめられました, meaning “was praised.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.why.2: ✗ (c) ほめて: ほめて is the て-form of ほめる and normally needs います or いました after it; it does not form the passive expression ほめられました.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q12.why.3: ✗ (d) ほめ: ほめ is the verb stem of ほめる, but it is missing られ, which is needed to make the passive form ほめられる here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.why.0: ✗ (a) むりで: むりで is the connective form of むりだ, usually used to connect to another clause or action, so it cannot end the clause directly before と 思う here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.why.1: ✗ (b) むりに: むりに is an adverb meaning “forcibly” or “reluctantly,” so it cannot function as the predicate in むりに と 思う.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.why.2: ✓ (c) むりだ: むりだ is the plain affirmative form of the な-adjective むり, and it correctly comes before と 思う to mean “think that it is impossible.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q13.why.3: ✗ (d) むりな: むりな is used before a noun as a modifier, but と 思う follows the blank here and there is no noun for むりな to modify.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.why.0: ✓ (a) すい: すい is the stem of すう after removing ます from すいます, so it correctly combines with すぎる to form すいすぎ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.why.1: ✗ (b) すう: すう is the dictionary form and cannot be directly followed by すぎる in this grammar pattern; すうすぎ is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.why.2: ✗ (c) すって: すって is the て-form of すう, but the て-form is not used before すぎる; すってすぎ is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q14.why.3: ✗ (d) すった: すった is the past form of すう, but it cannot be used before すぎる; すったすぎ is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.why.0: ✗ (a) 集まる is an intransitive verb meaning “to gather” or “to come together,” so it cannot directly take the object ごみを in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.why.1: ✗ (b) 集める is the correct transitive verb in meaning, but its dictionary form cannot come before おいて; it must be changed to the て-form, 集めて.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.why.2: ✗ (c) 集まって is the て-form of 集まる, meaning “come together,” but the trash does not gather by itself; someone needs to collect it.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q15.why.3: ✓ (d) 集めて is the て-form of 集める, meaning “collect/gather,” so it correctly goes with ごみを and combines with おいて.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.why.0: ✗ (a) ばかり — ばかり means “only/all” or “just recently,” so あさってばかり cannot express the deadline for returning the book.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.why.1: ✗ (b) まで — まで means “until” and usually indicates an ongoing period, so あさってまで does not clearly state that the book must be returned by the day after tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.why.2: ✗ (c) ばかりに — ばかりに means “just because” and usually gives a reason for a negative result, so it does not fit the polite request あさってばかりに返してください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q16.why.3: ✓ (d) までに — までに means “by” or “no later than,” and it marks the deadline for completing an action, so あさってまでに返してください is correct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.why.0: ✗ (a) など: など means “and so on” or “such as” and usually follows a noun; どこなど does not express the meaning “anywhere” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.why.1: ✓ (b) でも: When でも follows an interrogative word such as どこ, it forms どこでも, meaning “anywhere”; therefore, this sentence says that the speaker can sleep anywhere.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.why.2: ✗ (c) か: どこか means “somewhere,” but it does not express the meaning “anywhere” here, and connecting どこか directly with ねられます is not appropriate in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q17.why.3: ✗ (d) は: は marks a topic or contrast; putting it after どこ to make どこは does not fit the meaning or structure of this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.why.0: ✓ (a) で: In 大きい字で書いてください, で indicates the manner of writing, meaning “write in larger characters,” so it is correct.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.why.1: ✗ (b) が: が normally marks the subject, but 大きい字が書いてください does not express the manner of writing and is grammatically incorrect here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.why.2: ✗ (c) か: か is used to form questions or express alternatives, so it cannot connect 大きい字 with 書いてください in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q18.why.3: ✗ (d) や: や is used to list nouns such as “A and B, etc.”, so it cannot indicate the manner of writing in 大きい字で書いてください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.why.0: ✗ (a) を: を marks the object of an action, as in そうじを, so it cannot follow 友だち to identify the person performing the action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.why.1: ✗ (b) に: に usually marks a recipient, target, or direction, but 友だち is the person who performed the helping action here, so に is not used.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.why.2: ✓ (c) が: が marks 友だち as the subject, meaning that the friend performed the action そうじをてつだってくれた.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q19.why.3: ✗ (d) で: で usually marks the place or means of an action, so it cannot mark 友だち as the subject in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.why.0: ✗ (a) ごろ: ごろ means “around” and is used after a point in time, such as 5時ごろ, but あと5分ごろありません cannot express that only five minutes remain.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.why.1: ✓ (b) しか: しか means “only” and must be used with the negative form ありません; あと5分しかありません means “there are only five minutes left.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.why.2: ✗ (c) だけ: だけ also means “only,” but あと5分だけありません is not a natural way to express the remaining time in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q20.why.3: ✗ (d) で: で can mark a period of time in some structures, but あと5分でありません cannot mean “there are no more than five minutes left”; the correct structure here is しかありません.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.why.0: ✗ (a) くださいます: 「くださいます」 means that another person gives or does something for the speaker, so it cannot express “I will deliver” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.why.1: ✗ (b) なさいます: 「なさいます」 is the honorific form of 「します」 and is used for another person’s action, not for the speaker’s own action of delivering the parcel.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.why.2: ✗ (c) ございます: 「ございます」 means “to exist” or “to have” and is a polite form of 「あります」, so it cannot combine with 「おとどけ」 to express the action of delivering.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q21.why.3: ✓ (d) いたします: 「いたします」 is the humble form of 「します」; 「おとどけいたします」 means “I will deliver it” or “I shall deliver it,” which matches the subject 「私が」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.why.0: ✗ (a) みたい: みたい usually follows a noun to mean “like” or “seems like,” but this sentence needs the adverbial form みたいに to modify べんきょうしなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.why.1: ✗ (b) みたいな: みたいな modifies a noun that follows it, but the word after the blank is the verb べんきょうしなさい, so みたいな cannot be used here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.why.2: ✓ (c) らしく: らしく is the adverbial form of らしい and means “in a way befitting” or “characteristically”; 学生らしく naturally modifies べんきょうしなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q22.why.3: ✗ (d) らしい: らしい is the basic form used as a predicate or before a noun, whereas the adverbial form らしく is required before べんきょうしなさい.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.why.0: ✓ (a) 来たら: 来たら is the ～たら form of 来る and means “if/when he comes,” so it naturally combines with かならず私に知らせてください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.why.1: ✗ (b) 来ると: 来ると usually expresses an automatic or inevitable result, or something that happens whenever someone comes, and it does not naturally come before the request 知らせてください.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.why.2: ✗ (c) 来たり: 来たり is the ～たり form, which is used to list actions together with another ～たり form and usually する, so it cannot stand alone as the conditional expression here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q23.why.3: ✗ (d) 来るまま: 来るまま does not form a suitable conditional expression; ～まま usually means “leaving something as it is” or “while remaining in a state,” which does not fit the meaning “when Kobayashi comes.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.why.0: ✗ (a) にの: 「にの」 is not a correct combination in this sentence; the particle 「に」 cannot be directly combined with 「の」 to modify 「りゅうがくせい」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.why.1: ✗ (b) から: 「から」 means “from,” but when it directly modifies the noun 「りゅうがくせい」, it must be followed by 「の」 to form 「アジアからのりゅうがくせい」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.why.2: ✓ (c) からの: 「からの」 connects 「アジア」 to 「りゅうがくせい」 and means “students from Asia.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q24.why.3: ✗ (d) に: 「に」 usually marks a destination, time, or target, so 「アジアにりゅうがくせい」 does not mean “students from Asia” and does not fit the required structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.why.0: ✗ (a) は: だれは does not naturally express a request for “someone” to close the window; は marks a topic and does not turn だれ into an indefinite pronoun.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.why.1: ✗ (b) が: だれが means “who,” but だれがまどを閉めてください is not the correct form for this request; だれか is needed to mean “someone.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.why.2: ✓ (c) か: だれか means “someone/anyone,” so だれか、まどを閉めてください。 means “Someone, please close the window.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t26-q25.why.3: ✗ (d) に: に cannot follow だれ to express “someone” in this sentence; だれに usually means “to whom” or “with whom,” which does not fit the request to close the window.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.why.0: ✓ (a) に: 花にしましょう uses the pattern 〜にする, with に marking the chosen option; the sentence means “let’s choose flowers as the present.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) が: が marks the subject, but 花がしましょう does not express the meaning “choose flowers” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) を: を marks a direct object, but 花をしましょう is not the correct connection for expressing “choose flowers.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) も: も means “also,” but 花もしましょう would mean “also do flowers,” which does not fit the idea of deciding on a present.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.why.0: ✗ (a) ながら: ながら means “while doing...” and is usually attached to the verb stem, so it cannot follow 楽しかった旅行のこと in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.why.1: ✓ (b) ばかり: ばかり follows 楽しかった旅行のこと and means “only” or “nothing but,” forming 楽しかった旅行のことばかり思い出しています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.why.2: ✗ (c) しか: しか also means “only,” but it must be used with a negative predicate; since 思い出しています is affirmative, 楽しかった旅行のことしか思い出しています is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q2.why.3: ✗ (d) までに: までに means “by” or “before” and expresses a deadline, but this sentence is about remembering the enjoyable trip, not about a time limit.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.why.0: ✗ (a) へ: へ marks a direction or destination, so it cannot mark 母 as the person made to cry in 母へ泣かせる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.why.1: ✓ (b) を: を marks the person affected by the causative form 泣かせる; 母を泣かせる means “make my mother cry.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.why.2: ✗ (c) に: に can mark the person who performs an action in some causative patterns, but with the intransitive verb 泣く here, the person made to cry takes を, not に: 母に泣かせる is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q3.why.3: ✗ (d) の: の shows possession or connects nouns, so it cannot connect 母 with the verb 泣かせる in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.why.0: ✗ (a) が: Using only が after 飛んでいる would produce 飛んでいるが見えます, which does not form the required nominalized-subject structure with 見えます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.why.1: ✗ (b) を: を cannot directly connect 飛んでいるを見えます, because 見えます is an intransitive verb and does not take a direct object marked by を.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.why.2: ✓ (c) のが: の turns 飛んでいる, “are flying,” into a noun-like phrase, and が marks this visible event in 飛んでいるのが見えます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q4.why.3: ✗ (d) のを: のを normally marks the object of a transitive verb such as 見ます, but 見えます does not use のを in this structure.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.why.0: ✓ (a) だけ: 「半分だけ食べます」 means “I will eat only half,” which fits the speaker’s stomachache.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.why.1: ✗ (b) しか: 「半分しか」 must be used with a negative predicate, such as 「半分しか食べません」, so 「半分しか食べます」 is incorrect.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.why.2: ✗ (c) も: 「半分も食べます」 suggests “eat as much as half” or “also eat half,” rather than limiting the amount to only half.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q5.why.3: ✗ (d) と: 「と」 cannot connect 「半分」 to 「食べます」 to express “eat only half” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.why.0: ✓ (a) ならべて — ならべて is the て-form of ならべる, meaning “to arrange,” and it correctly connects with おきます in ならべておきます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.why.1: ✗ (b) ならんで — ならんで is the て-form of ならぶ, meaning “to line up” or “to be arranged in a line”; it is intransitive, so it cannot take おさらを in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.why.2: ✗ (c) ならべる — ならべる is the dictionary form, but the て-form is required before おきます to make the pattern ならべておきます.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q6.why.3: ✗ (d) ならぶ — ならぶ is the dictionary form of the intransitive verb meaning “to line up” or “to be arranged in a line”; it cannot connect directly to おきます and does not work with おさらを.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.why.0: ✓ (a) やめない: やめないつもりです uses the pattern “verb in the nai-form + つもりです,” meaning “intend not to do something”; the speaker intends not to quit their job.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.why.1: ✗ (b) なめたい: なめたい means “want to lick/taste,” so it is unrelated to やめる and does not express an intention not to quit the job in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.why.2: ✗ (c) やめよう: やめよう is the volitional form, meaning “let’s quit” or “I will quit,” but this sentence requires やめる or やめない before つもりです, not やめよう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q8.why.3: ✗ (d) やめたくない: やめたくない means “do not want to quit,” but やめたくないつもりです would mean “intend not to want to quit,” rather than directly expressing the intention not to quit the job.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.why.0: ✗ (a) おっしゃりて: 「おっしゃる」 does not form the て-form by combining 「おっしゃり」 with 「て」; the correct form is 「おっしゃって」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.why.1: ✓ (b) おっしゃって: This is the correct て-form of 「おっしゃる」 and combines correctly with 「ください」 in 「おっしゃってください」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.why.2: ✗ (c) あっしゃい: 「あっしゃい」 is not a correct conjugated form of the honorific verb 「おっしゃる」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q9.why.3: ✗ (d) おっしゃり: 「おっしゃり」 is a continuative stem form and cannot directly precede 「ください」 to make a request in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.why.0: ✗ (a) べんりで: べんりで is the conjunctive form of a な-adjective, but it cannot be followed directly by ので as べんりでので in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.why.1: ✗ (b) べんり: べんり is only the stem of the な-adjective, so it is missing な before ので; the correct form is べんりなので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.why.2: ✓ (c) べんりな: べんりなので is the correct combination of the な-adjective べんり and ので, expressing the reason “because it is convenient.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q10.why.3: ✗ (d) べんりだ: べんりだ is a sentence-ending form, but it cannot be used directly as べんりだので; it must change to べんりなので.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.why.0: ✗ (a) 強く: 強く is the continuative/adverbial form of 強い, normally used before a verb or another connecting structure, so it cannot directly precede だろう here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.why.1: ✓ (b) 強い: 強い is the plain present form of the い-adjective and can directly connect to だろう to express the prediction that the wind will be strong tomorrow.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.why.2: ✗ (c) 強くて: 強くて is the て-form of 強い, used to connect clauses or give a reason, so it is not appropriate immediately before だろう.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q11.why.3: ✗ (d) 強いと: 強いと forms a construction with と, usually meaning “if/when” or introducing quoted content, so 強いとだろう is grammatically incorrect in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.why.0: ✗ (a) みがけば: 「みがけば」 means “if you brush your teeth,” expressing a condition rather than the obligation required by 「〜なくてはいけません」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.why.1: ✗ (b) みがかないで: 「みがかないで」 means “without brushing your teeth,” and it does not combine naturally with 「いけません」 here to express “must brush your teeth.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.why.2: ✗ (c) みがいても: 「みがいても」 means “even if you brush your teeth,” expressing concession rather than the obligation intended in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q12.why.3: ✓ (d) みがかなくては: 「みがかなくては」 is a shortened form of 「みがかなくてはいけません」, meaning “must brush your teeth,” so it fits the sentence exactly.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.why.0: ✗ (a) くらい: くらい indicates an approximate amount or degree, so けがをした人くらい出ました does not express the meaning “injured people also appeared.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.why.1: ✓ (b) も: も follows けがをした人 and means “also,” showing that besides houses burning, injured people appeared as well.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.why.2: ✗ (c) とか: とか is used to give examples such as “things like…,” but けがをした人とか出ました does not clearly express the additive meaning “also” required here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q13.why.3: ✗ (d) か: か means “or” or shows uncertainty; けがをした人か出ました does not fit the grammar or meaning of this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.why.0: ✗ (a) とか: 「とか」 is generally used to give examples such as “like...” or to list items incompletely, so it cannot express an approximate depth of 10 meters here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.why.1: ✗ (b) とが: 「とが」 does not form a suitable grammar pattern after 「１０メートル」 and does not mean “about.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.why.2: ✗ (c) へは: 「へは」 marks direction or a topic, so it cannot connect with 「１０メートル」 to express an estimated depth.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q15.why.3: ✓ (d) ほど: 「ほど」 follows 「１０メートル」 to indicate an approximate amount, forming 「１０メートルほど」, meaning “about 10 meters.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.why.0: ✗ (a) ご覧: ご覧 is an honorific expression used for another person’s act of seeing, so 私もご覧いたしました cannot humbly describe the speaker’s own action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.why.1: ✓ (b) 拝見: 拝見する is the humble form of 見る and can be used in 拝見いたしました, meaning “I respectfully read/looked at it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.why.2: ✗ (c) お見: お見 cannot be followed by いたしました in this sentence; the honorific expression お見になります is used for a respected person’s action, not for the speaker’s humble action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q16.why.3: ✗ (d) 読まれ: 読まれ is the passive or honorific form of 読む, but 読まれいたしました is an incorrect combination and does not express the speaker’s humble action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.why.0: ✓ (a) でも: 小学生でも means “even an elementary school student,” which fits the sentence’s emphasis on how easy the problem is.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.why.1: ✗ (b) なのに: なのに means “although... but...,” expressing a contrast; 小学生なのにできる does not fit the intended meaning here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.why.2: ✗ (c) とか: とか is used to list examples such as “... or ...,” so 小学生とかできる cannot express the meaning “even an elementary school student can do it.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q17.why.3: ✗ (d) なので: なので means “therefore” or “because,” connecting a reason with a result; 小学生なのでできる would mean “can do it because they are an elementary school student,” which is not the meaning of this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.why.0: ✗ (a) いていたあいだに: 「いていた」 is a past form referring to a period of having been in Japan, but this sentence expresses an intention to visit a friend during a future stay.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.why.1: ✓ (b) いるあいだに: 「いる」 is the non-past form of 「いる」, and 「あいだに」 means “during the time when,” correctly showing that the one-time visit will happen while the speaker is in Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.why.2: ✗ (c) いていたあいだは: 「いていた」 has a past meaning, and 「は」 makes the period a topic or contrast; neither fits this sentence about a future intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q18.why.3: ✗ (d) いるあいだは: 「いる」 has the correct tense, but 「は」 usually emphasizes or contrasts the whole period, whereas a one-time action such as 「一度たずねたい」 calls for 「に」 in 「あいだに」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.why.0: ✗ (a) 悪くて: 「悪くて」 is the て-form of 「悪い」, mainly used to connect clauses or express a cause, not to form the conditional required after 「もし」 here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.why.1: ✗ (b) 悪くても: 「悪くても」 means “even if it is bad” and expresses concession, so it changes the intended conditional nuance of the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.why.2: ✓ (c) 悪ければ: 「悪ければ」 is the ば-form of 「悪い」 and means “if it is bad,” correctly forming the pattern 「もし～ければ」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q19.why.3: ✗ (d) 悪くも: 「悪くも」 is not the complete conditional form of 「悪い」; the correct conditional form is 「悪ければ」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.why.0: ✗ (a) に: 「あと５分に」 is not natural for expressing the remaining time before the meeting ends.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.why.1: ✓ (b) で: 「あと５分で」 means that an event will happen in five minutes; here, it means the meeting will end.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.why.2: ✗ (c) をしている: 「あと５分をしている」 is grammatically incorrect because 「をしている」 must follow an activity or action being performed.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q20.why.3: ✗ (d) まで: 「あと５分まで」 is unsuitable because 「まで」 marks a limit meaning “until,” while this sentence needs to express when the meeting will end after five minutes.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.why.0: ✗ (a) 寝た: 寝た means “slept” or “went to sleep,” describing a completed action rather than clearly showing that the cat was sleeping when the closet was opened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.why.1: ✗ (b) 寝る: 寝る is the dictionary form meaning “to sleep” or “will sleep,” so it does not fit a sentence describing the cat’s state at a past moment.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.why.2: ✓ (c) 寝ていた: 寝ていた is the past form of Vている and means “was sleeping,” which correctly describes the cat’s state when the closet was opened.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q21.why.3: ✗ (d) 寝たいんだ: 寝たいんだ means “wants to sleep” with an explanatory nuance, so it does not say that the cat was actually sleeping in the closet.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.why.0: ✗ (a) 続けてから — 続けてから means “after continuing to walk,” expressing a sequence of events rather than the sense that walking excessively will lead to collapsing.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.why.1: ✗ (b) 続けても — 続けても means “even if one continues walking,” creating a concessive meaning; this sentence does not mean “even if…, still…,” but says that walking too long will cause the speaker to collapse.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.why.2: ✓ (c) 続けては — 続けては expresses that continuing to walk for too long will lead to the undesirable result 倒れてしまう, meaning “collapse.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q22.why.3: ✗ (d) 続けたと — 続けたと cannot naturally connect to 倒れてしまう in this sentence; ～たと normally needs a pattern such as ～たと思う or ～たとき.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.why.0: ✗ (a) 行っては: 「行っては」 usually expresses repeated actions or a condition such as “if one goes,” so it cannot express “no matter where” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.why.1: ✗ (b) 行くなら: 「行くなら」 means “if someone is going” or “if someone plans to go,” which gives a specific condition rather than the meaning “wherever she goes.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.why.2: ✗ (c) 行ったら: 「行ったら」 means “if/when someone has gone” or “after going,” expressing a condition or time sequence, not the general idea “no matter where she goes.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q23.why.3: ✓ (d) 行っても: 「行っても」 is the て-form 「行って」 plus 「も」; with 「どこへ」, 「どこへ行っても」 means “no matter where she goes,” which fits the whole sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.why.0: ✗ (a) 男とか女とか: 「とか」 is used to list examples or possibilities vaguely, so 「男とか女とか分からなくなる」 does not correctly express “not knowing whether the person is male or female.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.why.1: ✗ (b) 男だった女だったり: This form is grammatically incorrect because 「～たり～たりする」 must be written as 「男だったり女だったり」; in addition, it describes alternating states or actions rather than uncertainty between male and female.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.why.2: ✓ (c) 男なのか女なのか: 「～なのか～なのか」 means “whether it is male or female,” which fits perfectly with 「分からなくなる」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q24.why.3: ✗ (d) 男だろう女だろう: 「だろう」 expresses conjecture or assumption, so 「男だろう女だろう分からなくなる」 does not form a natural either-or expression in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.why.0: ✗ (a) もう寒くない: This means “it is no longer cold,” which contradicts the idea of まだ寒い, meaning “it is still cold.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.why.1: ✓ (b) まだ寒い: This means “it is still cold,” which fits もう春になったのに, meaning “although it has already become spring.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.why.2: ✗ (c) もう暖かくなった: This means “it has already become warm,” so it does not create the contrast required by the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t27-q25.why.3: ✗ (d) まだ暖かい: This means “it is still warm,” but the sentence needs to say that it is still cold despite the arrival of spring.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.why.0: ✓ (a) 言われた: This is the past passive form of 言う, meaning “was told” or “was advised”; 孫に言われたので means “because I was told/advised by my grandchild.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.why.1: ✗ (b) 言わせた: This is the past causative form, meaning “made or let someone say”; 孫に言わせたので would mean “because I made my grandchild say it,” which does not fit the intended meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.why.2: ✗ (c) 言っている: This is the progressive form, meaning “is saying”; 孫に言っている usually means “is saying/telling something to the grandchild,” not that the speaker was told by the grandchild.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q1.why.3: ✗ (d) 言わない: This is the present negative form, meaning “does not say” or “will not say”; 孫に言わないので means “because I do not tell my grandchild,” which is the opposite of the intended meaning.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.why.0: ✓ (a) でも: 「だれにでも」means “to anyone/to everyone”; the pattern 「疑問 từ + に + でも」expresses an unlimited range, so it fits this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.why.1: ✗ (b) では: 「だれにでは」is not a natural expression in this sentence; 「では」does not mean “anyone” like 「でも」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.why.2: ✗ (c) ほど: 「だれにほど」is not a correct connection; 「ほど」usually expresses degree or comparison, so it cannot create the meaning “to anyone” here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q2.why.3: ✗ (d) ほか: 「だれにほか」is not a correct grammar pattern; 「ほか」usually means “other” or “besides” and cannot replace 「でも」in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.why.0: ✗ (a) ご覧する: ご覧する is not the standard respectful form of 見る; this sentence requires ご覧になる to honor the people viewing the picture.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.why.1: ✗ (b) ご覧いたす: ご覧いたす is not a correct expression here; いたす is the humble form of する and cannot be combined this way to honor the viewer’s action.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.why.2: ✗ (c) ご覧される: ご覧される is not the standard fixed honorific form needed here; the correct form is ご覧になる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q3.why.3: ✓ (d) ご覧になる: ご覧になる is the respectful form of 見る and appropriately describes the people who will view the picture before 方.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.why.0: ✗ (a) 考えてもかまいません: 「〜てもかまいません」 means “it is all right to〜,” so this choice would allow thinking only of oneself, which conflicts with the idea of also thinking about others.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.why.1: ✗ (b) 考えたほうがいいです: 「〜たほうがいいです」 means “should〜,” so 「自分のことばかり考えたほうがいいです」 would mean “one should think only of oneself,” contrary to the following sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.why.2: ✓ (c) 考えてはいけません: 「〜てはいけません」 means “must not〜,” so 「自分のことばかり考えてはいけません」 correctly expresses that one must not think only of oneself.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q4.why.3: ✗ (d) 考えなくてはなりません: 「〜なくてはなりません」 means “must〜,” so this choice would mean “must think only of oneself,” which contradicts 「人のことも考えなければならない」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.why.0: ✗ (a) 食べられる means “can eat” or “be eaten,” so it does not express that the speaker is forced to eat fish every day.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.why.1: ✓ (b) 食べさせられる is the causative-passive form of 食べる, meaning “be forced to eat,” which fits the complaint in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.why.2: ✗ (c) 食べたがる means “want to eat” and is generally used to describe another person’s desire, not being forced to eat as in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q5.why.3: ✗ (d) 食べすぎる means “eat too much,” but this sentence emphasizes being forced to eat only fish every day, not eating an excessive amount.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.why.0: ✗ (a) 食べなくて: 食べなくて is the negative て-form of 食べない and is generally used to connect a cause or state; in this sentence, it does not naturally express “went to bed without eating.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.why.1: ✗ (b) 食べずで: 食べずで is an incorrect connection; the pattern meaning “without doing something” is 食べずに, not 食べずで.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.why.2: ✗ (c) 食べないが: 食べないが means “does not eat, but…” and requires a contrasting clause; it does not express the intended meaning of going to bed without eating dinner.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q6.why.3: ✓ (d) 食べずに: 食べずに is a negative pattern meaning “without eating”; 食べずに寝ました means “went to bed without eating.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.why.0: ✗ (a) 楽しい: The final い in 楽しい is retained, so it cannot be directly followed by そうに; it must become 楽しそうに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.why.1: ✗ (b) 楽しくて: 楽しくて is the て-form of 楽しい, used to connect clauses or express a reason, not before そうに in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.why.2: ✓ (c) 楽し: 楽し is the stem of 楽しい after dropping い, so it correctly combines with そうに to form 楽しそうに.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q7.why.3: ✗ (d) 楽しく: 楽しく is the adverbial form of 楽しい, but 楽しくそうに is not a valid combination; the pattern ～そうに requires the adjective stem 楽し.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.why.0: ✓ (a) 痛かったし — 「痛かった」 is the past form of the i-adjective 痛い, and 「し」 adds the headache as another symptom alongside having a fever.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.why.1: ✗ (b) 痛かったが — 「が」 means “but” and expresses contrast; this sentence lists two symptoms, so the additive 「し」 is appropriate instead.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.why.2: ✗ (c) 痛いので — 「痛い」 is the non-past form, and 「ので」 means “because”; this does not match the past-time expression 「きのう」 in the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q8.why.3: ✗ (d) 痛かくても — 「痛かくても」 is an incorrect conjugation; if 「ても」 were used, the correct form would be 「痛くても」, meaning “even if it hurts.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.why.0: ✗ (a) だれかいませんでした: だれか means “someone,” so it does not naturally express “there was nobody” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.why.1: ✗ (b) だれかいました: だれかいました means “someone was there,” which contradicts the context that the speaker arrived 30 minutes too early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.why.2: ✓ (c) だれもいませんでした: だれも followed by the negative いませんでした means “nobody was there,” which fits the context of arriving too early.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q9.why.3: ✗ (d) だれもいました: だれも can mean “everyone” in an affirmative context, but this meaning conflicts with the situation and the sentence does not naturally express the intended idea.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.why.0: ✗ (a) します: 「顔をします」 can describe making an expression, but 「明るい顔をします」 is less suitable here than 「明るい顔をしています」 because the sentence describes her current state after passing the exam.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.why.1: ✗ (b) やります: 「やります」 means to do or carry out something, and it does not naturally combine with 「顔を」 to describe a bright expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.why.2: ✓ (c) しています: 「明るい顔をしています」 means that she has or is showing a bright, cheerful expression, which fits her happiness after passing the exam.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q10.why.3: ✗ (d) やっています: 「やっています」 means to be doing or carrying out something, so it is not used with 「明るい顔を」 to describe a person’s expression.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.why.0: ✗ (a) ありそうだ: 「元気がありそうだ」 means “he looks energetic or healthy,” which is the opposite of the meaning needed here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.why.1: ✗ (b) なそうだ: 「なそうだ」 is not the correct form; the correct form of 「ない」 with 「そうだ」 is 「なさそうだ」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.why.2: ✗ (c) あるみたいだ: 「元気があるみたいだ」 means “he seems healthy or full of energy,” which does not match the speaker’s concern about him.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q11.why.3: ✓ (d) ないみたいだ: 「元気がないみたいだ」 means “he seems not to be well,” which fits the following sentence 「どうしたんだろう」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.why.0: ✓ (a) なってきた: 「～てくる」describes a change that has progressed from the past to the present; 「悪くなってきた空気」means the air has gradually become worse and is now causing trouble.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.why.1: ✗ (b) なっていった: 「～ていく」emphasizes a change continuing from the present into the future or moving away from the reference point; 「悪くなっていった」does not fit the sentence’s focus on the present situation.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.why.2: ✗ (c) しておいた: 「～ておく」means doing something in advance as preparation; 「悪くしておいた」would mean intentionally making the air or atmosphere bad beforehand, which does not fit this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q12.why.3: ✗ (d) してあった: 「～てある」describes a resulting state caused by someone’s intentional action; 「悪くしてあった」does not naturally express the air becoming bad in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.why.0: ✓ (a) 泳げません: This is the polite negative form of the potential form 泳げる, meaning “cannot swim”; with １００メートルしか, it means “cannot swim more than 100 meters.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.why.1: ✗ (b) 泳ぎません: This is the polite negative form of 泳ぐ, meaning “do not swim” or “will not swim,” so it does not express a limit on swimming ability here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.why.2: ✗ (c) 泳がないです: This is a conversational negative form of 泳ぐ, meaning “do not swim,” not the negative form of the potential verb 泳げる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q13.why.3: ✗ (d) 泳げないそうです: This means “I hear that someone cannot swim” or “it seems that someone cannot swim,” adding reported information and conflicting with わたしは水泳ができますが in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.why.0: ✗ (a) 誘えて: 誘えて does not express “was invited”; it is not the passive form needed for 誘う in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.why.1: ✗ (b) 誘おう: 誘おう is the volitional form, meaning “let’s invite” or “I will invite,” so it cannot describe me being invited by Suzuki.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.why.2: ✗ (c) 誘わせて: 誘わせて is the て-form of the causative 誘わせる, meaning “let/make someone invite,” not “was invited” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q14.why.3: ✓ (d) 誘われて: 誘われて is the passive て-form of 誘う, meaning “was invited,” and it naturally connects the invitation with 楽しく過ごした, “had a good time.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.why.0: ✗ (a) 書くでしょう uses the dictionary form「書く」with「でしょう」to make a prediction that someone will write, but it does not clearly express the ability to finish the report within the limited time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.why.1: ✗ (b) 書くでしょうか asks whether someone will write using「書く」, but it does not convey the meaning “will it be possible to write it?” required by the context of only three days remaining.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.why.2: ✗ (c) 書けるでしょう uses「書ける」to express ability, but「でしょう」makes it a prediction rather than a direct question; this sentence requires「でしょうか」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q15.why.3: ✓ (d) 書けるでしょうか combines the potential form「書ける」with「でしょうか」to politely ask whether the report can be completed within three days.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.why.0: ✓ (a) 答えさせられて: This is the causative-passive form of 答える, meaning “to be made to answer,” so it correctly describes わたし being required by the teacher to answer a question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.why.1: ✗ (b) 答えせられて: 答えせられて is an incorrect conjugation; 答える must become 答えさせられる, not 答えせられる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.why.2: ✗ (c) 答えされて: 答えされて is not the correct causative-passive form of 答える; the causative element させ is needed to form 答えさせられる.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q16.why.3: ✗ (d) 答えられて: 答えられて usually means “can answer” or “be answered,” and it does not clearly express that わたし is forced to answer the teacher’s question.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.why.0: ✓ (a) 見続ける: 「見続ける」 means “to continue watching,” which fits 「長い時間」 and connects naturally with 「〜と」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.why.1: ✗ (b) 見出し: 「見出し」 usually means “headline,” so it is not the verb meaning “to continue watching” required here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.why.2: ✗ (c) 見たくなる: 「見たくなる」 means “to come to want to watch,” which does not express the cause of the eyes becoming painful.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q17.why.3: ✗ (d) 見にくい: 「見にくい」 means “difficult to see/watch,” so it does not describe watching TV continuously for a long time.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.why.0: ✗ (a) おもしろいそうではない: おもしろい cannot be directly combined with そうではない to express “does not look interesting”; the correct form is おもしろくなさそうだ.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.why.1: ✗ (b) おもしろいみたいではない: おもしろいみたいではない has the nuance “it is not that it seems interesting,” and is less natural here than おもしろくないみたいだ; it also does not match the そうだ pattern being tested.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.why.2: ✓ (c) おもしろくなさそうだ: おもしろい changes to the negative form おもしろくない, and そうだ is then used to express the appearance “looks uninteresting.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q18.why.3: ✗ (d) おもしろくずだ: おもしろくず is not a correct conjugated form of the adjective おもしろい, so it does not make a valid grammatical pattern.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.why.0: ✗ (a) はずではない: 「あきらめるはずではない」 means “should not be expected to give up” or “is not supposed to give up,” expressing an expectation rather than the speaker’s intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.why.1: ✓ (b) つもりはない: 「あきらめるつもりはない」 means “have no intention of giving up,” which exactly expresses the speaker’s determination in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.why.2: ✗ (c) 予定ではない: 「あきらめる予定ではない」 says that giving up is not part of the plan or schedule, but it does not clearly express the speaker’s personal resolve.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q19.why.3: ✗ (d) 場合はない: 「あきらめる場合はない」 means “there is no situation in which one would give up,” referring to a circumstance rather than a personal intention.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.why.0: ✗ (a) なくなって: 「なくなる」is an intransitive verb meaning “to be lost” or “to disappear,” so it cannot take the object 「大切な手帳を」 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.why.1: ✓ (b) なくして: 「なくす」means “to lose” and can take 「大切な手帳を」 as its object; 「なくして」 expresses that losing the notebook led to 「困っていた」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.why.2: ✗ (c) なくなれば: 「なくなれば」is the conditional form of 「なくなる」, meaning “if it is lost” or “if it disappears,” but this sentence describes an actual cause, not a hypothetical condition.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t28-q21.why.3: ✗ (d) なくすれば: 「なくすれば」is the conditional form of 「なくす」, meaning “if someone loses it,” but it does not fit 「困っていた」 because the sentence reports a past situation caused by an event that actually happened, not a condition.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.why.0: ✗ (a) おいちゃ: 「おいちゃ」 is a shortened form of 「置いては」, but it does not form the 「～ておいていい」 pattern meaning “it is okay to leave something as it is” in this sentence.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.why.2: ✓ (c) おいといて: 「おいといて」 is the casual form of 「置いておいて」, meaning “leave it as it is,” which fits the idea that the trash will be thrown away later.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q3.why.3: ✗ (d) おいた: 「おいた」 is the past form of 「置く」, meaning “put/left,” so it does not express permission to leave the trash as it is in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.why.0: ✗ (a) こう: こう means “in this way/like this,” so こう簡単に does not express the intended degree of “so easily” in this sentence.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q4.why.3: ✗ (d) それ: それ is a pronoun meaning “that thing/that matter,” and it cannot directly combine with 簡単に to mean “so easily.”

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q5.why.3: ✗ (d) 集まっていらっしゃいます: 集まる is incorrect because the postcards do not gather by themselves, and いらっしゃいます is also inappropriate for the subject わたし.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.why.0: ✗ (a) それら: それら means “those things” and normally refers to plural nouns, so it cannot modify うまくいく in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.why.1: ✗ (b) どれら: どれら relates to “which ones” and does not express the degree to which 仕事はうまくいく, so it does not fit this sentence.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q7.why.3: ✗ (d) こんな: こんな means “this kind of” or “like this” and normally comes before a noun, but this sentence needs a degree expression before うまくいく, so こんなに is required.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.why.0: ✓ (a) いないで: 「見ていないで」 uses the pattern 「～ないで」 to tell the listener to stop just watching TV and do homework, which fits 「宿題をしなさいな」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q8.why.1: ✗ (b) いて: 「見ていて」 uses 「いて」, the affirmative progressive form of 「いる」, so it suggests continuing to watch TV or doing something while watching TV, contrary to the instruction to do homework.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.why.2: ✓ (c) から: から means “from” and marks a source or starting point; 毎日の生活の中からも means “also from within everyday life.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q10.why.3: ✗ (d) を: を usually marks an object or a route, but 毎日の生活の中をも does not correctly express “learning from everyday life” in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q11.why.0: ✗ (a) 出よう: 出よう is the volitional form, meaning “let’s attend” or “I will attend,” so 出ようはありません is not the correct way to express “I have no intention of attending.”

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q15.why.3: ✗ (d) ほか: ほか means “another” or “besides,” and does not express the choice of a larger apple in this sentence.

default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q17.why.2: ✗ (c) だったら: 「話だったら」 means “if it was that story/information,” so it expresses a condition instead of indicating the source of information.
