default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.why.1: ✓ (b) 見たいと思っています: 見たいと思っています expresses that 息子 continues to have the desire to watch オリンピック大会 after going to London.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.why.2: ✗ (c) 見たいです: 見たいです is commonly used to state the speaker’s direct desire; with 息子, it is less natural here than 見たいと思っています.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q18.why.3: ✗ (d) 見たがると思っています: 見たがる describes an outwardly shown tendency or desire, while 見たがると思っています sounds unnatural for stating 息子’s specific desire in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.why.0: ✗ (a) 来るはずはありません: It means “he cannot be expected to come,” which contradicts 来ると言ってあります, meaning that he has said he will come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.why.1: ✓ (b) 来ないはずはありません: It means “it cannot be that he will not come,” which fits the statement that Yamada has said he will come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.why.2: ✗ (c) 来るほうがいいです: It means “it is better to come” and expresses advice, not an inference based on 来ると言ってあります.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q19.why.3: ✗ (d) 来ないほうがいいです: It means “it is better not to come,” which is advice that conflicts with Yamada’s statement that he will come.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.why.0: ✗ (a) そうに: そうに usually follows the stem of an adjective or a verb to express appearance or signs, so it cannot directly follow the noun 今年 in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.why.1: ✗ (b) らしくて: らしくて expresses something being characteristic of or typical of this year, but 今年らしくて暑いと does not express the intended meaning “as hot as this year.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.why.2: ✓ (c) みたいに: 今年みたいに means “like this year,” and みたいに can modify 暑い to form the phrase “as hot as this year.”
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q20.why.3: ✗ (d) のようで: After 今年, のようで forms 今年のようで, meaning “like this year and...” or “seeming like this year,” so it does not directly modify 暑い in this structure; for this comparison, のように is needed: 今年のように.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.why.0: ✗ (a) らしく: 田中さんらしく usually means “in a way characteristic of Tanaka” and does not naturally express “a person like Tanaka” before 優しい人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.why.1: ✗ (b) みたいに: みたいに is an adverbial form, so it cannot directly modify the noun 優しい人; to say “a kind person like Tanaka,” use 田中さんみたいな優しい人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.why.2: ✓ (c) のような: 田中さんのような means “like Tanaka,” and のような can directly modify the noun 優しい人, so it fits the sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q21.why.3: ✗ (d) だそうな: だそうな expresses hearsay or an apparent fact, not the comparison “like Tanaka,” and it does not fit the structure 田中さん（　　）優しい人.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.why.0: ✗ (a) ように generally expresses a desired goal or result, but 習う is a deliberate action by the speaker, so ために is more natural and accurate here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.why.1: ✓ (b) ために follows the dictionary-form verb 習う to express the purpose “in order to learn”; the speaker came to Japan for the purpose of learning genuinely natural Japanese.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.why.2: ✗ (c) かわりに means “instead of” or “in exchange for,” so it cannot express the purpose of coming to Japan to learn Japanese in this sentence.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q22.why.3: ✗ (d) ままに means “as it is” or “according to,” so it cannot connect with 習う to express the purpose of coming to Japan.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.why.0: ✗ (a) ほうに: 「ほうに」usually indicates a direction, side, or preference, so it cannot express the reason Yamada was absent because of illness.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.why.1: ✓ (b) ために: 「病気のために」means “because of illness” or “due to being sick,” expressing the reason Yamada could not attend the meeting.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.why.2: ✗ (c) ものに: 「ものに」does not form an expression of cause in this sentence; it normally appears in other patterns such as 「ものだ」or 「ものの」.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q23.why.3: ✗ (d) ところに: 「ところに」indicates a time or place when something happens, so it does not mean “because of illness” here.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.why.0: ✗ (a) では: 「寒いでは思いませんでした」 cannot use 「では」 to connect the adjective 「寒い」 with 「思いませんでした」 when expressing the content of a thought.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.why.1: ✗ (b) には: 「寒いには思いませんでした」 does not use 「には」 to mark the content being thought about; 「には」 usually indicates an object, purpose, or contrast.
default.q.2026_bunpou_n4-t29-q24.why.2: ✓ (c) とは: 「寒いとは思いませんでした」 uses 「とは」 to quote and emphasize the content “cold,” forming the pattern 「～とは思いませんでした」.
